response.query: What consent wording and HR/supervisor procedures will safeguard voluntariness and prevent coercion when collecting supervisor ratings?
response.answer: To safeguard voluntariness and prevent coercion in supervisor ratings, use clear, voluntary consent wording and ensure HR/supervisors emphasize participation is entirely voluntary and won't affect employment.

results.title: Consent Process Best Practices for Special Populations to ...
results.content: The study team should not include the student’s professor as a member, since potential participants may be concerned that they will receive a bad grade or other punishment if they do not agree to enroll in the research. For example, recruitment for research involving an anonymous survey could take place in person, but the study team could request a waiver of documentation of consent so participants will not have to provide their names on forms linking them to their participation. When conducting research in participant populations that are more susceptible to feeling pressure to participate, study teams need to be mindful of regulatory requirements and adopt a consent process that minimizes this pressure. Depending on the circumstances, this may require additional consent disclosures, identifying different individuals to conduct recruitment and obtain consent, changing the consenting setting, relying on the participation of an LAR, or designing the research procedures to limit who on the study team knows who participated. A well-developed consenting process will reduce a participant’s perceived pressure to enroll in the study.

results.content: Sincerely, Original signed by Steven Mackay Director Negotiations Branch Employee Relations and Negotiations Division Centre for Public Sector Labour Relations and Compensation Treasury Board Secretariat c: Deputy Chris Harkins, Deputy Commissioner, Field Operations, Ontario Provincial Police Marnie Clark, Director, People Operations, Career Development Bureau, Ontario Provincial Police 139 Letter of Intent No. 20 – Specialist Positions in the North Letter of Understanding Between The Crown in Right of Ontario (Management Board of Cabinet) “the Employer” and Ontario Provincial Police Association ‘the Association” RE: Specialist Positions in the North The Employer and the Association confirm that a Uniform member, who is in a specialist position in either Northeast or Northwest Region and has completed a minimum of 7 continuous years in their specialist position, shall be entitled to submit a lateral transfer request to a frontline position in any location and shall be treated as a Duration complete member for the purposes of determining priority status only.
